name: M2
dof_breakdown: 3 per hip, 1 per knee, 2 per ankle
summary: The Leg Lab's attempt to take Spring Flamingo's force-controlled walking off the boom and into three dimensions: twelve actuated joints, Series Elastic Actuators, Virtual Model Control and machine learning. Its stated goals were as much about engineering discipline as locomotion — walk 1 m/s, work nine attempts out of ten, become a 'robotic workhorse' that could be experimented on without breaking. It stood under its own battery power in 2000; in 2001 the project moved with Gill Pratt to Olin College.
notable: Series Elastic Actuation and Virtual Model Control carried into a full 3D biped
Reliability as an explicit design goal, unusual for a research machine of its day
Followed Gill Pratt to Olin College in 2001, closing out the Leg Lab's biped line
